title: Grok Build overview
claims: Grok Build supports interactive TUI, headless use and ACP.
Its headless output can be streaming JSON.
notes: No local install or ACP session was tested.

tool: Grok Build is now open source
title: Grok Build is now open source
claims: xAI announced that Grok Build’s coding agent and TUI were open-sourced.
notes: License and repository revision need direct verification before use.

title: ZCode repository
claims: The public Apache-2.0 repository includes desktop, web, backend, CLI and runtime source.
notes: Source was not built or audited.

title: ZCode Agent
claims: ZCode documents workspace context, execution modes and goal-mode completion/state recovery.
notes: Data and network policy were not tested.

title: Warp Agents overview
claims: Warp documents local/CLI/cloud agent surfaces, approval and diff review, parallel conversations and a cloud automation platform.
notes: Cloud isolation/lifecycle details require separate verification.

title: Warp products overview
claims: Warp documents terminal, agent, automation platform and Factory product layers.
notes: Product overview only.

title: Jules FAQ
claims: Jules is a public-beta asynchronous coding agent.
Each task runs in a fresh VM that clones a repository and installs dependencies.
notes: No VM execution was tested.

title: TRAE Agent and IDE windows
claims: TRAE documents distinct Agent and IDE workspaces.
The Agent workspace can manage multiple tasks and hand long tasks to cloud execution.
notes: Chinese official documentation; policy details not established.

title: oh-my-pi
claims: oh-my-pi identifies itself as a Pi fork and documents a coding-agent package, in-process tools and worktree-isolated subagents.
notes: Canonical OMP source selected in the final sweep; downstream forks are excluded from canonical identity claims.

title: Command Code Docs
claims: Command Code documents CLI and desktop surfaces and broad model support.
notes: Marketing performance claims excluded; lifecycle and licensing unresolved.

title: What is Tabby
claims: Tabby is an open-source self-hosted coding assistant with deployment, editor extension and API documentation.
notes: Agent behavior requires separate verification.

title: Plandex repository
claims: Plandex presents itself as an open-source terminal agent for large multi-step coding work.
notes: No plan/edit lifecycle was tested.

title: Tabnine Agent
claims: Tabnine distinguishes autonomous Agent from chat and documents developer check-ins for input or approval.
notes: Closed product; plan-specific governance needs review.

title: Refact archive
claims: The original Refact repository is archived and identifies a successor development home.
Refact Cloud is stated as retired.
notes: Do not treat archive as active integration target.

title: Amazon Q Developer Documentation
claims: Amazon Q documents IDE/CLI workspace context and an agent that can plan, implement and test approved work.
notes: Service policies require AWS-specific review.

title: Flowise introduction
claims: Flowise documents visual Assistant, Chatflow and Agentflow builders, orchestration, logging, evaluations and MCP support.
notes: General workflow platform, not a coding harness claim.

title: Open-AutoGLM README
claims: Open-AutoGLM is a phone agent framework using ADB and vision-language control.
It documents confirmation for sensitive operations and manual takeover.
notes: Excluded from coding-harness corpus; retained as computer-use lead.

title: OpenViking repository
claims: OpenViking describes a context/memory/knowledge/skills database and coding-agent plugin integration.
notes: Deduplicated to context lane.

title: RTK
claims: RTK describes filtering/compressing tool output before it enters agent context across supported coding agents.
notes: Deduplicated to context lane.

title: Pi
claims: Pi presents itself as a minimal extensible agent harness with extensions, skills, prompt templates, themes and packages.
The coding-agent README documents interactive, print/JSON, RPC and TypeScript SDK modes.
notes: Canonical active source; badlogic/pi-mono redirects here. The previously cited pi-packages source was a mirror.

title: oh-my-pi
claims: oh-my-pi identifies itself as a fork of Pi and documents its own package, in-process tools and worktree-isolated subagents.
notes: Canonical OMP source; downstream forks are not treated as separate canonical candidates.

title: vLLM OpenAI-compatible server
claims: vLLM documents an OpenAI-compatible serving interface and warns that its API-key option does not protect every endpoint.
notes: Provider endpoint, not a coding agent; no deployment was tested.

title: AutoCodeRover
claims: AutoCodeRover describes repository-structure-aware autonomous program improvement.
notes: Research/tooling lineage; maintenance and operational controls were not evaluated.

title: Agentless
claims: Agentless documents localization, repair and patch-validation phases.
notes: Research system, not evidence of a durable interactive harness.

title: OpenACP
claims: OpenACP presents a self-hosted ACP bridge/control surface for sessions and messaging endpoints.
notes: No channel authentication or dispatch behavior was tested.

title: Iris Agent
claims: Iris presents CLI, HTTP, ACP, LSP and MCP surfaces for a local coding agent.
notes: Source claims only; no protocol session was run.

title: ZAP Coding Agent
claims: ZAP presents a local Rust coding agent with AST indexing, skills and ACP v1 support.
notes: ACP compatibility was not independently tested.

title: Octomind
claims: Octomind documents CLI, JSONL, daemon/WebSocket and ACP surfaces over one session engine and an optional working-directory sandbox.
notes: Package/tap installation and sandbox enforcement were not tested.

title: San
claims: San presents a Go terminal runtime with configurable prompts, tools, providers, extensions, MCP and replay inspection.
notes: Performance and update claims were not tested.

title: Heddle
claims: Heddle documents a TypeScript runtime/SDK with durable runs, approvals, artifacts and an optional separate execution host.
notes: The execution-host contract is documented as experimental.

title: AX Code
claims: AX Code documents structured event logs and file snapshots for review, run comparison and rollback.
notes: Unreleased computer-use capability was not treated as available.

title: Terminuz
claims: Terminuz presents a local terminal coding agent with provider support, MCP and user-facing permission-aware tool execution.
notes: Maintenance and permission enforcement were not independently tested.

title: ACP-Bridge
claims: ACP-Bridge documents an OpenAI-compatible local-model to ACP bridge with working-directory-scoped tools and opt-in web allowlisting.
notes: Its stated test/compatibility results were not rerun.

title: acpr
claims: acpr fetches the ACP registry and launches a selected agent using its declared distribution method.
notes: Launcher download and execution were not tested.

title: ACP Router
claims: ACP Router documents ACP-registry discovery, worktree dispatch, job/session/event tracking and cancellation.
notes: Its documented default bypass-permission setting is a policy risk, not an endorsed default.

title: Auggie CLI
claims: Auggie documents interactive and print automation modes, ACP support and GitHub workflow integration.
notes: Closed product; retention and authorization policies were not retrieved.

title: ACP Registry
claims: The ACP Registry documents a curated agent index with CI validation, distribution metadata and hourly release update checks.
notes: Registry inclusion is not an independent security or lifecycle endorsement.

title: Synapse Agent
claims: Synapse presents a terminal-first local coding agent with persistent goals, visible tool/context state and token-aware tool-output handling.
notes: A distinct product despite its Deep Agents foundation; no runtime was tested.

title: DeerFlow
claims: DeerFlow presents a long-horizon agent harness with sandboxes, memory, skills, subagents and a message gateway.
Its documentation describes an allowlist for commands used by stdio MCP servers.
notes: The source calls its allowlist defense in depth, not a security boundary.

title: DeepSeek-Reasonix
claims: DeepSeek-Reasonix is a public CLI and desktop coding-agent repository.
Its documentation describes a DSH subagent integration and configurable local state.
notes: Reliability and enforcement claims were not tested.

title: fx
claims: fx documents a Zig native coding-agent CLI with ACP, skills, MCP and project instructions.
It exposes an embeddable libfx surface.
notes: Repository labels fx experimental; no capability was tested.

title: Gajae-Code
claims: Gajae-Code documents a Bun/TypeScript coding CLI with Rust-native components and agent, tools, TUI, session, SDK, workflow, LSP and daemon subsystems.
notes: Architecture contract only; no release or runtime test was performed.

title: jcode
claims: jcode presents a Rust coding-agent harness for multi-agent workflows with swarms and self-development features.
notes: Comparative performance statements were not independently evaluated.

title: nanobot
claims: nanobot presents a self-hosted personal-agent framework with tools, memory, MCP and multi-agent workflows.
notes: Adjacent general-agent runtime, not a coding-specific harness.

title: GPT Researcher
claims: GPT Researcher presents an autonomous deep-research agent and documents MCP configuration.
notes: Research/workflow peer; no repository-edit authority is inferred.

title: Local Deep Researcher
claims: Local Deep Researcher presents a fully local web research and report-writing assistant.
notes: Research assistant, not a coding loop.

title: MiroThinker
claims: MiroThinker presents an open deep-research agent for complex research and prediction tasks.
notes: Reported benchmark numbers were not adopted as study results.

title: Weft
claims: Weft compiles one capability into multiple harness-native manifests and documents lockfiles, eval artifacts and publication gates.
notes: Compiler output must remain subject to host capability policy.

title: Moatless Tools
claims: Moatless Tools is the attributable upstream repository for the previously queued Moatless identity.
notes: Mechanism and lifecycle were not deeply reviewed.

title: Mentat archive
claims: The former Mentat CLI repository is archived and read-only.
notes: Not an active integration target.

title: SandBase Harness
claims: SandBase Harness documents local, Docker, Kubernetes and worker sandbox backends, resumable event streams, MCP toolsets, permission policy and a TypeScript SDK.
notes: Provider and sandbox behavior were not tested; local process is not a strong isolation boundary.

title: TrueForge
claims: TrueForge presents itself as an open-source agent-harness runtime layer.
notes: Detailed execution and policy semantics were not evaluated.

title: agents-wire
claims: agents-wire presents an ACP-based TypeScript SDK for local coding-agent sessions, including budgets, permission middleware and orchestration.
notes: Normalization does not prove or add backend enforcement; no adapter was run.

title: Andbo
claims: Andbo documents a policy-controlled container sandbox with egress policy, secret redaction, audit sessions, MCP and skills integration.
Its local runtime does not enforce network policy.
notes: No container, cluster or policy was run.

title: a2acode
claims: a2acode maps ACP coding-agent sessions to A2A while preserving progress, diffs, permission prompts and session context.
notes: The server inherits agent-authentication context; no deployment was tested.

title: Open Agent Bridge
claims: Open Agent Bridge documents a shared local registry, MCP adapter, A2A server and SQLite-backed channel-message acknowledgements for coding-agent sessions.
notes: Session injection and identity boundaries were not tested.

title: Pipelock
claims: Pipelock documents mediated HTTP, WebSocket, MCP and A2A traffic inspection with signed action receipts.
Its documentation limits receipts to traffic that crosses the mediation boundary.
notes: Core and multi-agent tiers have different licenses; no policy or receipt was executed.

title: aMaze Control Plane
claims: aMaze documents proxy-side policy enforcement for LLM, MCP and A2A traffic, including tool visibility filtering and traces.
notes: Operator hardening and proxy deployment were not evaluated.

title: OpenHand
claims: OpenHand documents an LLM-agnostic agent platform with plugin tools and sandbox policy.
Its documented same-UID sandbox and in-process plugins are not OS-level isolation.
notes: No runtime or plugin was executed.

title: MCP Agent Security Gateway
claims: MCP Agent Security Gateway documents default-deny inspection of routed MCP/JSON-RPC tool calls with audit and policy checks.
It describes itself as an engineering research prototype and limits enforcement to supported routed paths.
notes: Current license is all rights reserved; no gateway was run.

title: Agent Security Harness
claims: Agent Security Harness is a published CI action/package for protocol-level MCP/A2A endpoint tests.
Its documentation distinguishes inconclusive unreachable or unserviced targets from passing controls.
notes: No endpoint or benchmark was run.

title: ToolHive
claims: ToolHive documents a gateway, registry and runtime for managed MCP servers, with container deployment and per-request identity and access policy when configured.
notes: Container and network enforcement were not tested.

title: CUGA Agent
claims: CUGA documents a configurable open-source generalist agent harness from IBM Research with a LangGraph-based orchestrator, policy, skills, tools and optional sandbox capabilities.
notes: No CUGA runtime was installed or exercised.

title: Docker MCP Gateway
claims: Docker MCP Gateway documents an MCP CLI gateway with registry references, profiles, tool enablement and secrets or OAuth handling.
notes: No gateway or server image was run.

title: Fleet
claims: Fleet documents a governed runtime where file and shell operations execute in a container data plane with policy, audit and cancellation/retirement behavior.
notes: Containment and cancellation behavior were not independently tested.

title: EdgeF MCP Gateway
claims: EdgeF MCP Gateway documents authenticated, namespaced MCP tool routing with per-client policy, quotas and redacted SQLite audit.
notes: No upstream process or policy was run.

title: MCP Gateway & Registry
claims: MCP Gateway & Registry documents asset discovery, registration admission control, authentication, authorization, skill allowlists and audit.
notes: Deployment and operational claims were not independently tested.

title: Every Code
claims: Every Code is an Apache-2.0 community fork of Codex with browser and MCP integration, multi-agent commands, approval modes and workspace sandboxing.
notes: Fork lifecycle and safeguards were not tested.

title: Youtu-Agent
claims: Youtu-Agent documents automatic generation of agent configuration and tool code from a described capability.
notes: Generated code and configuration were not run or audited.

title: CodeBuddy Code quickstart
claims: CodeBuddy documents CLI project use and Chinese, international and enterprise login routes.
notes: Closed product; deployment and privacy behavior were not tested.

title: SynapseOrch documentation
claims: SynapseOrch documents agents, DAG workflows, MCP tools, skills, durable memory, approval policy, resumable runs and sandboxed Python.
Its docs distinguish self-hosted AGPL and cloud operation.
notes: Distinct identity from Synapse Agent; no self-hosted deployment was run.

title: cplt
claims: cplt documents kernel-level sandboxing for several coding agents, explicit environment pass-through and repository-held sandbox policy.
notes: Platform and agent-specific limitations were not exercised.

title: Harnss
claims: Harnss documents a desktop ACP client with built-in Claude Code and Codex engines, registry agents, MCP configuration and permission levels.
It documents that prebuilt binaries are unsigned.
notes: No desktop client or agent was installed.

title: BOSS
claims: BOSS documents a loopback MCP tool surface for coding CLIs, signed plugins, RBAC and per-tool toggles.
Its documentation states plugins are in-process rather than OS-sandboxed.
notes: No plugin, RBAC deployment or MCP tool was run.

title: Agentic Harness
claims: Agentic Harness documents append-only replayable thread state, playbooks, budget controls, review loops and MCP support.
Its alpha documentation marks several planned capabilities as incomplete.
notes: No LLM workflow or control was exercised.

title: AgentGUI
claims: AgentGUI documents a Node ACP client with WebSocket synchronization, SQLite persistence and direct local-agent daemon management.
notes: No daemon or persisted session was used.

title: ACP Agent Hub
claims: ACP Agent Hub documents VS Code, CLI and mobile clients for ACP-compatible coding agents and a mobile WebSocket relay.
notes: Relay authentication and deployment controls were not tested.

title: Codewhale
claims: Codewhale documents a terminal coding agent with selectable action approvals, plugins/MCP, local or hosted model endpoints and Fleet multi-agent support.
Its product page identifies codewhale-hq/CodeWhale as the canonical source.
notes: Provider credential handling and approval enforcement were not tested.

title: Docker Agent
claims: Docker Agent documents YAML-configured root and sub-agents with separate contexts and built-in or MCP tools.
Docker documents that versions 4.49 through 4.62 called the feature cagent.
notes: Image/runtime isolation semantics were not tested.

title: Vibe Kanban
claims: Vibe Kanban is a public repository for orchestrating coding agents in dedicated worktrees.
notes: Worktree orchestration does not itself establish process, credential or network isolation.

title: VibeTree
claims: VibeTree documents parallel terminal coding-agent tasks, one git worktree per task, persistent terminals and desktop, web and CLI surfaces.
notes: Release/update and host authorization behavior were not tested.

title: Agetor
claims: Agetor documents per-task git worktrees and tmux sessions for installed coding CLIs, with structured transcripts and surfaced approvals.
Its repository labels several harness integrations experimental.
notes: It drives underlying CLIs and was not evaluated as an isolation boundary.

title: HAR
claims: HAR documents a CLI and MCP harness for agent worktrees with deterministic launch, verification and teardown stages.
It documents per-slot worktrees, ports and optional databases plus recorded verification evidence.
notes: Coordination mechanisms were not tested as an OS-level isolation boundary.

title: tclaude
claims: tclaude documents a local daemon that wraps multiple coding CLIs with durable sessions, identity, permissions, audit and automation.
It documents sandbox/network-filter profiles using bubblewrap, Seatbelt or a harness sandbox.
notes: Operating-system and platform enforcement were not tested.

title: agentmux
claims: agentmux documents durable per-agent queues, tmux or native agent sessions, structured logs and a Discord ChatOps bridge.
notes: Its autonomous launch configuration and external channel expand the authority boundary.

title: conduct
claims: conduct documents a local TUI for parallel coding-agent worktrees, diff review and explicit approvals for shell or network actions.
It documents persisted workspace metadata while an agent process does not survive a restart.
notes: No process lifecycle or approval behavior was tested.

title: omux
claims: omux documents a generic spawn/send/confirm/await agent adapter, push-based waiting and per-agent MCP scoping.
Its documentation describes parallel isolation as panes and working directories rather than git worktrees.
notes: No supervision, memory or permission behavior was tested.

title: Software Factory
claims: Software Factory documents labeled GitHub-issue intake, leased worktree CLI-agent runs, independent validation and a separate publication decision.
It documents that lease expiry is not a process fence and retains selected worktrees for inspection.
notes: Its documented test and live-run results were not repeated in this research.

title: Jackalope
claims: Jackalope documents a prerelease desktop workspace for installed coding agents, parallel worktrees, task-owned browser sessions and review queues.
It explicitly states that worktrees isolate Git changes rather than operating-system privileges.
notes: Native task execution requires an approved account; no build or task was run.

title: Kith
claims: Kith documents scoped task claims, worktrees, port reservations, supervised command mutexes and explicit integration through MCP, CLI and editor surfaces.
Its documentation limits claims and hooks to coordination among cooperative clients, not filesystem sandboxing.
notes: Recorded validation was not treated as this research's test result.

title: Gluon Agent
claims: Gluon Agent documents a self-hosted Claude Code orchestrator with persistent sessions, worktrees, Docker/bubblewrap execution and CLI, web, Telegram and Discord control.
It documents host-mounted credentials for the containerized environment.
notes: Container and remote-control security behavior were not tested.

title: ADHDev
claims: ADHDev documents worktree nodes, an append-only local SQLite ledger and a test-gated Refinery integration flow.
Its standalone service is localhost-only by default and warns on unauthenticated LAN binding.
notes: Cross-machine/cloud behavior was not tested.

title: Artemis
claims: Artemis documents worktrees, explicit launch and workflow approvals, and main-process command revalidation.
Its public repository has no published tags or releases.
notes: Documented build/smoke evidence was not repeated and does not establish a current release.

title: Agent Deck
claims: Agent Deck documents an independently maintained self-hosted fork of sunset Vibe Kanban with restored board behavior, agent workspaces and local SQLite execution state.
Its board layer depends on a separate Postgres and ElectricSQL remote stack.
notes: No self-hosted instance or fork update path was tested.

title: Paseo
claims: Paseo documents a daemon/client system for coding-agent worktrees, plugins and optional device relay.
Its documentation warns that plugins run on the daemon machine and connected clients.
notes: Relay, plugin and multi-device authority boundaries were not tested.

title: pando
claims: pando documents a local daemon that creates worktrees and runs staged coding-agent jobs with deterministic evidence.
It documents no public API authentication and instructs operators not to expose its daemon.
notes: No daemon, credentials, job or PR path was exercised.

title: Agent Dashboard
claims: Agent Dashboard documents multi-host, containerized daemons, remote PTY access, YAML agent profiles and OpenTelemetry telemetry.
It documents optional worktree spawning for multiple agents on a repository.
notes: Remote terminal and daemon security behavior were not tested.

title: HyprDesk
claims: HyprDesk documents a router/worker desktop system over a local MCP/A2A tunnel with worktree isolation and merge-back review.
notes: Autonomous mode and embedded browser authority boundaries were not tested.

title: Agent Console
claims: Agent Console documents worktree sessions and MCP delegation, messaging and timer tools.
Its security documentation limits use to trusted local networks because it provides host terminal access.
notes: No MCP server or terminal session was used.

title: Stoneforge
claims: Stoneforge documents a Smithy agent orchestration runtime and Quarry event-sourced task SDK.
It documents durable workflow and handoff state with workers in isolated worktrees.
notes: Dispatch, merge and workflow behavior were not tested.

title: Detent
claims: Detent documents a GitHub Projects-driven coding-agent orchestrator with worktrees, validation gates and a serialized merge train.
notes: No board, worker, validation gate or merge train was exercised.

title: stefan1294 Agent Orchestrator
claims: Agent Orchestrator documents worktree-based feature tracks with implementation, verification and fix phases plus retry handling.
notes: Prompt, retry and merge policy were not tested.

title: buhuipao Agent Console
claims: buhuipao Agent Console documents a local terminal control plane for Codex, Claude Code and Pi with owned-process reconnection and Pi event forwarding.
It excludes fork-subagent and sidechain transcripts from its primary session discovery.
notes: Distinct from ms2sato/agent-console; no session integration was tested.

title: showagent
claims: showagent documents local discovery and conversion of supported coding-agent session stores into native sessions for another CLI.
Its MCP server can search, read and request a handoff while documented transcript output redacts common secrets by default.
notes: Session conversion, redaction and MCP disclosure behavior were not tested.

title: Agent TUI
claims: Agent TUI documents an Apache-2.0 packaging fork of Grok Build with one TUI core and provider runtime add-ons.
It documents interactive, headless and ACP modes and its own fork/release materials.
notes: Fork lifecycle, runtime behavior and supply-chain process were not tested.

title: Kandev
claims: Kandev documents terminal, ACP and provider-specific Codex app-server integration paths.
Its integration guidance distinguishes ACP, Codex app-server, REST/WebSocket and MCP as different boundaries.
notes: No agent integration or permission behavior was tested.

title: Zut
claims: Zut documents AGENTS.md layering, extensions, session persistence, bounded headless orchestration and interactive tool confirmation.
It documents that interactive confirmation is ignored in print, JSON and RPC modes.
notes: Provider, tool and confirmation behavior were not tested.

title: jayhf Agent Deck
claims: jayhf Agent Deck documents terminal session management, MCP and skills managers, worktree lifecycle and conductor automation.
Its documentation includes configurable automation paths that can use bypass-approval tool arguments.
notes: Distinct from the-niresh/agent-deck; no session, automation or sandbox was run.

title: llama.cpp server
claims: llama.cpp documents generation, embeddings and reranking endpoints, speculative decoding and router-mode model loading.
notes: Endpoint authorization, resource and model lifecycle behavior were not tested.

title: mlxcel
claims: mlxcel documents local generation, embeddings, reranking and entity redaction with multi-model routing and live LoRA support.
notes: Deployment, remote Web UI and model download behavior were not tested.

title: Zenith
claims: Zenith documents one orchestrator that decides worker/tester spawning, skill registration, replanning and stopping across MCP/ACP adapters.
notes: Its reported benchmark outcomes were not treated as study measurements.

title: AgentMemory
claims: AgentMemory documents CPU embeddings, Redis hybrid BM25/vector RRF, optional cross-encoder reranking and graph boosts delivered through MCP, HTTP and CLI.
notes: Rules, retention and remote endpoint authorization were not tested.

title: AgentLink
claims: AgentLink documents visible approvals, local lexical and structural retrieval, cross-provider review and MCP, skill and plugin surfaces in a VS Code harness.
notes: Desktop/CLI previews and platform/release behavior were not tested.

title: OpenHarness
claims: OpenHarness documents multi-machine native agent CLIs in tmux panes, a worktree per harness and peer-to-peer terminal transport.
notes: Remote device, relay and skill authority were not tested.

title: harnext and Context Engine
claims: harnext documents a terminal coding harness and a separate Context Engine that indexes and ranks organization events for agent context.
notes: Context ingestion, retention and access controls were not tested.

title: Xal
claims: Xal documents a beta MIT terminal harness with a headless core whose UI, providers, tools, LSP, MCP bridge, memory, skills and hooks are plugins.
notes: Plugin trust, updates and capability behavior were not tested.

title: AgentMux
claims: AgentMux documents an open-source desktop and mobile environment for local coding agents, terminals, memory and connectors.
It labels the product alpha and presents local-network mobile access.
notes: Distinct from adelost/agentmux; lifecycle and mobile-network behavior were not tested.

title: Cretli
claims: Cretli documents a self-hosted mobile PWA that mediates multiple coding harnesses through one WebSocket protocol and supports plan-to-executor handoff.
Its documentation says plan mode is not a sandbox.
notes: Shell, file and git operations run on the host and were not tested.

title: Libre Claw
claims: Libre Claw documents append-only JSONL runs, side-effect approvals, replay, a local daemon, web UI and Telegram bridge.
notes: Remote approval channels and provider export paths were not tested.
